quiz.title: Relations & Functions Miscellaneous Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight mixed questions covering types of relations, one-one and onto functions, composition, inverses and binary operations. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Relations and Functions miscellaneous exercise

questions.q: A relation R on set A is an equivalence relation if it is:
questions.explanation: An equivalence relation must satisfy all three properties together: reflexive, symmetric and transitive.

questions.q: The function f : R → R given by f(x) = 3x + 5 is:
questions.explanation: f(a) = f(b) forces a = b, so it is one-one, and every real y has a pre-image x = (y − 5)/3, so it is onto. Hence bijective.

questions.q: If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 3, then (g ∘ f)(x) equals:
questions.explanation: (g ∘ f)(x) = g(f(x)) = g(2x) = 2x + 3. Apply f first, then g.

questions.q: For a bijective function f, the composition (f ∘ f⁻¹)(x) equals:
questions.explanation: A function composed with its inverse gives the identity, so (f ∘ f⁻¹)(x) = x for every x in the range.

questions.q: The operation * on R defined by a * b = a + b − ab has identity element:
questions.explanation: We need a * e = a, so a + e − ae = a, giving e(1 − a) = 0 for all a, hence e = 0.

questions.q: The greatest integer function f(x) = [x] from R to R is:
questions.explanation: Many values such as 2.1 and 2.7 map to 2, so it is not one-one, and no non-integer is an image, so it is not onto.

questions.q: A relation R on Z defined by aRb if a − b is divisible by 5 is:
questions.explanation: a − a = 0 is divisible by 5 (reflexive), if 5 | (a − b) then 5 | (b − a) (symmetric), and divisibility is preserved on adding (transitive). So it is an equivalence relation.

questions.q: For a binary operation * on a set A, closure means that for all a, b in A:
questions.explanation: Closure requires the result a * b to remain inside the set A. Commutativity, associativity and identity are separate properties.

faq.q: What does the Relations and Functions miscellaneous exercise cover?
faq.a: It mixes every idea from the chapter: types of relations (reflexive, symmetric, transitive, equivalence), one-one and onto functions, composition of functions, invertible functions and binary operations. The problems combine these rather than testing them one at a time.

faq.q: How do you prove a function is invertible?
faq.a: Show it is both one-one (injective) and onto (surjective), which makes it bijective. Once that is established, the inverse exists; you then find it by solving y = f(x) for x in terms of y.

faq.q: What is the difference between a relation and a function?
faq.a: Every function is a relation, but a relation is a function only when each input is paired with exactly one output. In the miscellaneous exercise you often decide which category a given rule falls into.

faq.q: How do you find the identity element of a binary operation?
faq.a: Set a * e = a and a = e * a, then solve for e so the equation holds for every element of the set. If no single value works for all elements, the operation has no identity.
